epoch_ai.synthesis: Oct 30: Epoch reports that GLM 5.3, an open-weight model Z.ai released in August, autonomously built a working exploit against each of the six Firefox versions released Sept 17 to Oct 26, using only the security fixes Mozilla had published but not yet shipped to users (the 'patch gap'). Each attempt cost about $1,000 in compute, against more than $100,000 for the whole research effort; the fastest took 12 hours of a 48-hour limit. The newest versions needed a second, unpublished flaw chained in, which Epoch reported to Mozilla and which was patched in Firefox 159.0 on Oct 27. Read from the feed's summary of the longer report; the report was not read. Oct 26 (earlier): 'We tried to automate Epoch', where the leaders averaged 65% against human-employee rubrics. The cron's Epoch pull is 403-blocked; fetched directly.

semianalysis.synthesis: Nov 3: SemiAnalysis says SpaceX has about 3.6 GW under construction across several sites, two months after its 10 GW-in-2027 estimate drew pushback as infeasible. Nov 1: roughly three-quarters of the 33.8 GW due across its top 20 states is already under construction, which is why it holds to its global +50 GW year (Oct 16). Nov 2: it launched GDPx, a benchmark of frontier-model capability across high-value domains. Read from feed summaries only (paywalled); the capacity figures come from SemiAnalysis's own models, method undisclosed.

farmdoc_daily.synthesis: Nov 2: Cortarelli, Gardner and Colussi compare nine typical soybean farms (five US, four Brazil; agri benchmark data, 2020-2024). Total cost averaged $616 an acre in the US against $416 in Brazil, and the gap is overhead, mostly land ($251 against $97). Direct costs were close ($200 US, $218 Brazil): Brazil paid more for fertilizer ($85 against $57) and pesticides ($81 against $56), the US more for seed ($66 against $43). They conclude cutting inputs will not close the gap, and that Brazil's advantage narrows when imported-input prices rise (2023: $71). Five-farm and four-farm samples, so typical-farm illustrations, not national averages. Oct 29 (summary only): non-real-estate farm loan volume at commercial banks fell 25.0% year over year in Q3 2026 on smaller loans, while the number of originations rose.

drought_monitor.synthesis: Indiana as of Oct 27: 72.6% abnormally dry or worse (D0+), up from 51.1% on Oct 20, and 16.3% in moderate drought (D1), the first D1 this fall (0.0% in every earlier week back to Sept 22). D0+ coverage has gone 3.2% (Sept 22), 10.0%, 11.2%, 18.8%, 51.1%, 72.6%. The Nov 3 map was not yet in the pull.

nass_crop_progress.synthesis: Week ending Nov 1, Indiana: corn 75% harvested for grain (61% a week earlier, 46% two weeks earlier); soybeans 87% harvested (75%, 59%). This week's pull carries harvest only, not maturity or leaf-drop.

interconnection_fyi.synthesis: Indiana holds 56 tracked data-center projects (33 proposed, 13 cancelled, 6 under construction, 4 operational), unchanged in all 49 snapshots since Sept 12 (latest Nov 4). Lake (9) and Porter (7) counties lead.

noaa_ncei_monthly.synthesis: September 2026, Indiana, revised slightly (651 station-months, from 646): 71.1°F average and 3.2 in. precipitation, against 73.0°F and 7.2 in. for August; Michigan 62.2°F and 3.2 in. The pull carries no normals; MRCC's regional figure (+4.9°F) gives the departure.

equitable_growth.synthesis: Oct 30: an argued piece (Bangert-Drowns) says announced tariff escalation against Canada and the lack of a China deal end the summer's calm in trade policy; it argues tariff costs and uncertainty add to inflation already pushed by the war in Iran, strengthen the case for Fed rate hikes by year end, and could squeeze AI firms' financing for data centers. It cites the latest Beige Book's repeated mentions of tariff costs and calls on the next Congress to act. A policy argument, not a measured result. Oct 23 (earlier): an assessment of Sen. Wyden's unemployment-insurance bill, which found research on AI's labor-market effects mixed.

ipcc.synthesis: Nov 2: Working Group I authors meet in Arusha, Tanzania, Nov 2-6 to advance the AR7 physical-science report. Oct 29: the suspended 65th Plenary will resume virtually Dec 1-3, with two items remaining, including the Work Plan (the timelines for the AR7 reports and the budget were left unresolved on Oct 16). Oct 30: registration opened for expert review of the first-order draft of the 2027 methodology report on carbon dioxide removal and carbon capture. Read from feed summaries; the ipcc.ch pages refuse scripted fetches.

beige_book.synthesis: Oct 14, Chicago District: activity was flat on balance in late August and September, after rising slightly in the Sept 2 report. Consumer spending was flat; construction, real estate and business spending fell slightly; prices rose moderately and wages modestly; farm income expectations for 2026 fell slightly, after improving in September. Nationally, most Districts saw little or no change in consumer spending, and over half said spending was driven by high-income households.

indiana_dnr_water.synthesis: Indiana DNR, September: statewide rainfall 91% of normal, after 200% in August. Ten of 12 tracked streams ran above normal; the Muscatatuck River near Deputy was lowest at 16% of mean monthly flow. Groundwater was above normal at 4 of 9 wells, near normal at 3, and well below at LaGrange 2 and Clark 20. The seasonal outlook shows no drought through at least December.

fia_indiana.synthesis: USFS 2025 evaluation for Indiana: 4.83M acres of forest, 14.07B cu ft growing stock. Annual mortality is 1.18% of standing volume (sampling error 5.5%), essentially level with 1.19% in the 2024 evaluation; net growth is 2.23%. First reading in this series.

mrcc_monthly_summary.synthesis: September 2026: Midwest average 68.5°F, 4.9°F above the 1991-2020 normal, with the whole region above normal (August was +0.9°F). Read from the feed's opening paragraph; the MRCC site has returned errors on several pulls since Oct 18.

interconnection_fyi_national.synthesis: Across 46 US state pages the largest active pipelines are Virginia (329), Texas (282) and Ohio (86); Indiana is 4th at 39 (4.0% of 972) but 32nd in operating sites (4 of 2,435). These ranks are unchanged in every snapshot from Oct 20 to Nov 4. The tracker's own headline count moved again (13,027 on Oct 24, 13,131 on Nov 4) with no change on the state pages, and does not reconcile with them, so read ranks as rough.

epoch_datacenters.synthesis: Dataset updated Nov 2: 96 covered sites (95 a week earlier) and 15.1 GW (from 14.2); the US is 12.58 GW (from 12.01), 83%. Indiana is 3 sites and 1.22 GW, 8.1% of the covered total (Anthropic-Amazon New Carlisle 1,037 MW, Meta Jeffersonville 178 MW, Google Fort Wayne 0 MW). Covered set only, not world capacity.

ohchr_ukraine_civilians.synthesis: September 2026: the UN monitoring mission verified at least 328 civilians killed and 2,105 injured, 85% more than in September 2025, with casualties on 22 of the month's 30 days. Its head, Danielle Bell, said the first two weeks of October were among the deadliest periods for civilians in years. July had been the highest month since March 2022. Counts are verified cases and are revised upward later. Read via UN News; the OHCHR site refuses scripted fetches.

ochaopt_gaza.synthesis: Oct 29 report (week of Oct 19-25): the Gaza Ministry of Health, which operates under the de facto authorities, reported 33 killed and 188 injured Oct 20-26, bringing the total since the October 2025 ceasefire to 1,559 killed and 5,608 injured; 42 more deaths were added retroactively once identified. These are MoH and Israeli-authority figures the UN has not verified. Private-sector truck entries recovered to 343 (up 9% on the prior week's 315, when a halt was reported over a fee charged by the de facto authorities), and flour and fresh-product prices rose over 70% against Oct 12-18. The report describes arson, shootings and new cement blocks along the 'Yellow Line' displacing families. The cumulative total since October 2023 is in the Oct 28 snapshot PDF and was not read. The report does not state ceasefire terms.

ofac_sdn.synthesis: List file modified Oct 28: 19,484 entries (19,471 on Oct 21); 6,733 carry a Russia or Ukraine program tag, 4,070 an Iran tag, 3,360 SDGT (counter-terrorism, which covers Hamas but is not Gaza-specific), all three unchanged. A standing count: designations raise it and delistings lower it, so it reads week against week.

kiel_tracker.synthesis: Release 31 (Oct 8) adds aid announced through August 2026. Its headline is Germany: of the EUR 100 billion Germany reports as bilateral aid, about 41.7 billion counts as aid to Ukraine under Kiel's method, 35.9 billion was spent in Germany, largely on Ukrainian refugees, and 22.0 billion is future military commitments. Donor totals are in the release file and were not read this session.

ice_detention.synthesis: ICE's latest file (FY2026, data as of July 9, file dated July 20): 65,765 people in detention, 19,329 convicted of a crime, 20,247 with charges pending and 26,189 with immigration violations only, so 70.6% with no criminal conviction. ICE's detention page, updated Oct 27, still links the file dated July 20 on Nov 4, more than three months old. Fetched directly; ice.gov refuses the cron runner.

press_freedom_tracker.synthesis: 256 incidents against journalists from Jan 1 to Nov 4, 2026, against 287 in the same span of 2025, not counting chilling statements. Assaults lead (168), then arrests or criminal charges (45) and equipment damage (31); subpoenas or legal orders 22. Latest incident dated Oct 23; the count was 253 on Oct 27.

atlas_surveillance.synthesis: 15,135 records of police surveillance technology across 7,761 agencies, unchanged at Nov 4 from the first reading on Oct 22. Body-worn cameras 5,470, license-plate readers 4,094, drones 1,828, face recognition 980. Indiana: 410 records, of which 216 are license-plate readers, 110 body cameras and 38 drones. Slow-moving; an unchanged count is expected.

fec_money.synthesis: 2026 cycle through Oct 31: PACs, super PACs included, raised $12.51 billion and spent $5.45 billion (through Sept 30: $11.08 billion and $4.25 billion); candidates raised $3.26 billion and parties $1.98 billion. PAC money is not limited to independent expenditures, and spending by groups that do not disclose donors cannot be separated in this series.

justsecurity_litigation.synthesis: 992 court challenges to administration actions tracked, from the tracker page published Nov 3, up from 984 on Oct 26 and 983 on Oct 20. The tracker's rules count an appeal with its case and some groups of related suits as one. Fetched directly; the site refuses the cron runner.

ccc_protests.synthesis: Data through May 2026 (Dataverse version of Sept 10): 4,534 protest events in May, after 6,226 in January, 3,343 in February, 6,620 in March and 3,284 in April. Indiana: 128 in May, between 107 and 180 each month since December. The data runs about four months behind.

iranhr_executions.synthesis: October 2026: Iran Human Rights reports at least 77 people executed in the month (39 for murder, 31 for drug-related offences, 6 for security-related charges, 1 for rape) and 691 executions recorded in 2026. First reading in this series, so no month-on-month comparison yet. Read from the article's headline and opening line; the site refuses scripted fetches, so its counting method was not read.
